variantPolicy: Seeded variants alter traffic, telemetry freshness, dependency delay, and business ambiguity; variants are replay aids and not independent published assets.

exercises.title: Design a Journey-Centered Health Dashboard
exercises.objective: Create overview and diagnostic panels that support safe checkout decisions.
exercises.initialState: Synthetic traffic, success, latency, pool, JVM, dependency, deployment, and payment-state fixtures are available.
exercises.prompt: Define panel contracts, units, aggregations, freshness, owners, privacy, runbook links, and unknown states.
exercises.deliverable: Dashboard specification and acceptance test matrix.

hints.text: Start with the operational decision, not the metric catalog.
A panel needs a freshness and failure behavior.

exercises.referenceSolution: Use business success and eligible denominator on the overview, tail latency/error/traffic, resource and dependency panels for diagnosis, release markers, freshness/unknown state, privacy-safe dimensions, owners, and synthetic/target-runtime acceptance tests.

exercises.title: Diagnose JVM Versus Pool Saturation
exercises.objective: Rank competing performance hypotheses from a shared timeline.
exercises.initialState: Synthetic metrics show checkout p95, success, pool wait, heap, GC, CPU, worker use, and database contribution across a release window.
exercises.prompt: Produce a causal timeline, leading hypothesis, rejected alternatives, verification checks, and safe containment recommendation.
constraints: do not infer from one metric
exercises.deliverable: Evidence table and incident decision record.

hints.text: Pair resource evidence with the affected journey.

exercises.referenceSolution: Align windows, show pool wait preceding checkout tail latency, use trace/database contribution, reject JVM pressure if its indicators remain baseline, contain the bounded workload if permitted, and verify sustained technical and business recovery.

exercises.title: Fault-Inject a False-Green Dashboard
exercises.objective: Test dashboard behavior under missing and misleading telemetry.
exercises.initialState: A synthetic dashboard fills missing series with zero and marks zero traffic healthy.
exercises.prompt: Define fault injections, expected panel states, alert interactions, and recovery evidence for zero traffic, stale metrics, partial permissions, delayed ingestion, dependency outage, and ambiguous payment state.
exercises.deliverable: Fault-injection suite and corrected dashboard contract.
acceptanceCriteria: every fault has expected unknown/degraded state

hints.text: Test data absence separately from data value zero.
A healthy-looking panel can be a telemetry failure.

exercises.referenceSolution: Represent missing, stale, and unauthorized data as unknown/degraded; test zero traffic and denominator changes; preserve privacy; require synthetic or business verification; retain release/dependency context and deterministic replay evidence.
